text.p: Capral Aluminium Ltd said on Tuesday it would hold a board presentation in the next couple of months on its plans for co-investment projects in the Asia/Pacific region.
This would be followed by a phase of looking for co-investment with other partners in the region, Capral chairman Jeremy Davis told a media briefing after the annual general meeting.
"It could be quite some months or even indeed realistically the beginning of 1998 before we are in a position to say 'here is the project and here is the co-investor'," Davis said.
Capral has said previously it wants to use its key skills, especially in the downstream businesses, to invest in the Asia/Pacific region in a series of medium-size commitments.
Davis said the company was not looking at smelting or large-scale rolling investments, but was more interested in foil, extrusion and distribution.
Investments would tend to be incremental, perhaps in the order of A$50 million.
"We would anticipate on our current planning that we would be able to fund those out of operating cashflow," he said.
Davis also said the company's decision to pay a special fully franked dividend of 25 cents a share was designed to distribute franking credits as they were generated.
"In effect, we do not think it sensible to hoard excess capital against the possibility of an unanticipated opportunity 'turning up'," he told shareholders.
Davis said if a major investment emerged that required extra capital, the company would seek shareholder support at that time.
